sources.entry: d9 - Turn SQL databases into secure APIs through an intuitive admin interface. Data platform and headless CMS (fork of Directus). (Source Code) GPL-3.0 Nodejs

summary.one_liner: d9 is an independently maintained, GPLv3 fork of Directus 9 that turns SQL databases into REST and GraphQL APIs with a no-code admin interface.
summary.what_it_does: d9 layers a Node.js REST and GraphQL API over an existing or new SQL database and provides a Vue.js admin dashboard ("Data Studio") for managing the data without code. It supports PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, OracleDB, CockroachDB, MariaDB and MS-SQL. It is positioned as a fork of Directus 9 that keeps the same database schema, so Directus 9 projects can migrate by updating package names. Extensions written for Directus 9 are stated to work with d9. The project also offers an npm project template, a JS SDK, and a separate projen template (@wbce/projen-d9, Apache 2.0) with a d9-plumbing CLI that saves roles, permissions, flows, dashboards and settings into a repository and applies them to other environments. Permissions can be exported as Cedar policies. The README says the database commands in that CLI assume PostgreSQL.
use_cases: Expose an existing SQL database as a REST or GraphQL API
Give non-technical users a web admin panel for database records
Build a headless CMS on top of SQL
Migrate a Directus 9 project while keeping its schema
Keep d9 roles, permissions and config in version control across environments
stack: SQL databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, OracleDB, CockroachDB, MariaDB, MS-SQL)
notable: Independent GPLv3 fork of Directus 9, created after Directus 10+ became premium
Same database schema as Directus 9, so migration is a dependency change
Works with new or existing SQL databases without migration
Config-as-code CLI (d9-plumbing) that exports permissions to reviewable Cedar policies
Directus 9 extensions stated to be compatible
caveats: Based on Directus 9, so it does not include Directus 10+ features
The config-as-code database commands assume PostgreSQL, per the README
README states it is not affiliated with Directus or Monospace Inc.
